blocks.text: Forward Selection built a feature subset up gradually, starting from nothing and adding one feature at a time. Backward elimination takes the genuine, complete opposite approach, starting from every available feature and removing them one at a time instead, a mirror image strategy that reaches the same general kind of result from the other direction entirely.

This topic covers how backward elimination starts from the full feature set, how it evaluates every currently included feature for possible removal at each round using cross validation, a real, genuine advantage this direction has over forward selection, seeing the complete feature interactions from the very first round, a real, genuine cost that comes with starting so large, and the same underlying greedy limitation both strategies genuinely share.
1. Starting From Everything
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421233-562286257.png

Backward elimination genuinely begins with every single available feature already included in the set. This is genuinely the defining starting point that gives this strategy its name, tearing down from a complete set, in direct contrast to forward selection genuine starting point of nothing at all.
Starting full means the very first round genuinely has to identify which single feature, when removed, hurts real model performance the least, exactly the first concrete step covered next.
2. Trying Every Possible Removal
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421233-394169339.png

At every round, backward elimination genuinely takes every feature currently included in the set, and tries removing each one, individually, training an actual model and evaluating its genuine real performance using cross validation for every single candidate removal. If 10 features remain in the set, that genuinely means 10 separate models get trained and evaluated in that one round alone.

This is genuinely the exact mirror of the evaluation process covered in Forward Selection, the same real, wrapper method discipline, actual model performance driving every decision, just applied in the opposite direction, testing what happens when a feature leaves rather than when one joins.
3. Removing the Least Useful Feature Each Round

blocks.alt: Removing the Least Useful Feature Each Round
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421900-718291207.png

Once every genuine candidate removal has been tried for that round, whichever removal hurt real performance the least, or even genuinely helped it, gets carried out permanently, that feature leaves the set for good. The process then genuinely moves to the next round with one fewer feature remaining to consider for removal.

This genuine, permanent commitment at each step mirrors forward selection exactly, once a feature is removed, it is never reconsidered or added back later, the same real, greedy limitation covered directly further in this topic.
4. A Worked Example
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421901-108148311.png
Using scikit-learn SequentialFeatureSelector with the backward direction shows this entire process applied directly, on the exact same small dataset used in the previous topic.

code.content:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import SequentialFeatureSelector
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100, 2400],
    "bedrooms": [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1])

selector = SequentialFeatureSelector(
    LogisticRegression(), n_features_to_select=2, direction="backward", cv=3
)
selector.fit(X, y)

print("Selected features:", X.columns[selector.get_support()].tolist())

blocks.text: This starts from all three columns and genuinely removes shoe_size_unrelated first, since its removal genuinely hurts real performance the least, correctly arriving at the exact same square_feet and bedrooms result forward selection reached, just approached from the opposite direction.

blocks.text: 5. A Real, Genuine Advantage: Seeing Full Interactions From the Start

blocks.alt: A Real, Genuine Advantage: Seeing Full Interactions From the Start
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421902-565882234.png

Forward selection early rounds genuinely evaluate features largely in isolation, or in small, still growing combinations, since the set starts empty and builds up gradually. Backward elimination, by genuine contrast, starts its very first round already considering the complete feature set together, genuinely capturing every real interaction effect among all features from the very first evaluation onward.

This is a genuinely real, meaningful advantage in situations where important interaction effects, exactly the kind covered back in Interaction Features, only become visible when several features are genuinely present together, something forward selection early, isolated rounds could more easily miss entirely.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Backward elimination genuine advantage over forward selection is seeing every feature interaction from round one. This matters most when a real, important signal only emerges from several features genuinely being present together.

blocks.text: 6. A Real, Genuine Cost: An Expensive, Risky Start

blocks.alt: A Real, Genuine Cost: An Expensive, Risky Start
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421903-442539332.png

Training the very first model with genuinely every available feature included can be slow, especially with a genuinely large number of features, and can also become numerically unstable when the number of features approaches or exceeds the number of available training rows, a real, practical risk forward selection, which starts small, never faces in its early rounds.

This is a genuine, real tradeoff worth weighing directly against the interaction advantage covered above, backward elimination sees more from the start, but pays a real, genuine cost for that complete view right at the most demanding, expensive part of the entire process.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Strategy","Genuine First Round Cost"],"rows":[["Forward selection","Genuinely cheap, starts with a single feature at a time"],["Backward elimination","Genuinely expensive, starts by training on every feature at once"]]}

blocks.text: 7. The Same Greedy Limitation, Shared With Forward Selection

Exactly like forward selection, backward elimination genuinely commits permanently to each removal the moment it happens, with no ability to reconsider or add a feature back later. A feature removed early because it looked unhelpful on its own might genuinely have become valuable in combination with a feature removed even later, a possibility this greedy process can never revisit once that removal has already happened.

This shared, real limitation is genuinely worth remembering, both directions covered in these two topics are efficient, practical heuristics, not guaranteed searches for the single best possible feature subset that could exist.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Try both forward selection and backward elimination on the same dataset when computationally feasible, and compare their resulting feature subsets directly, since each can genuinely surface a slightly different, real answer.

blocks.text: 8. Backward Elimination Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Backward Elimination Versus What Comes Next
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421903-445918748.png

Forward Selection and Backward Elimination together cover the two genuine, opposite directions of greedy, step by step wrapper method search, each with its own real tradeoffs around cost and the ability to see feature interactions. Both, though, decide what to remove using genuine, but comparatively blunt, real performance drops alone.

The next topic, Recursive Feature Elimination, refines this genuine backward direction into something more systematic, using a model own internal feature rankings, its coefficients or importance scores, to decide what to remove at each step, rather than relying purely on measuring the performance change from each individual removal.

items: Backward elimination genuinely starts from the complete feature set and removes features one at a time.
At each round, every currently included feature is genuinely tried for removal and evaluated with cross validation.
The genuinely least harmful removal each round gets carried out permanently on the selected set.
This direction genuinely sees the complete feature interactions from its very first round, unlike forward selection.
Starting with every feature included makes the genuine first round more computationally expensive and potentially unstable.
The next topic, Recursive Feature Elimination, refines this backward direction using a model own internal feature rankings.
